commits.message:
Remove stale documentation and dead citations

Delete delivered plans, superseded designs, dated snapshots and diaries:
the 2026-10-01 public-testnet decision set, the event-history design and
delivery documents, the builder-consolidation plan, the module-size
refactor diary, the workflow funding measurements, the test-quality audit
and its delivered cards, two superseded research notes, the site's
duplicate runbook page and a settlement verification diary.

Cut the L1 architecture plan and the public-submit ingress design to their
outstanding work, and the watcher journeys, testing status, remaining gaps
and availability-challenge documents to what is current.

Correct the remaining documents, guides, skills and READMEs against the
source: commands, flags, paths, symbols, counts, statuses and journal
descriptions.

Remove citations of sections and labels that no longer exist from source
comments, test titles and a few internal messages. SQL migrations and the
follower's schema strings keep theirs because their bytes are checksummed,
as do the Aiken doc comments that the blueprint copies.

Dispute caches hold one run's values, not maps by header

A dispute workflow is built for one run over one header, so the caches of
admitted transactions, decoded outputs, resolve moves and referenced
outputs each held a single entry. They are plain values now, and the
comments say they last for the run, not the process. The named units stay
keyed by header: naming a unit under a header is what holds its history.

Move deploy, release and devnet tooling to the hub-oracle policy id

Release signing signs the manifest content and the release bindings, deploy tooling stops writing manifestId, the public node is given MIDGARD_PUBLIC_HUB_ORACLE_POLICY_ID, and readiness, storage and acceptance checks compare hubOraclePolicyId. The watcher journeys' raw L1 double derives its rollback cursor from the request.

Not run here: the live watcher journeys and ten container tests, which need Docker.

Refuse a manifest file that differs from the signed manifest

The classifier's manifest file, a completed workflow's manifest, the family runtime's manifest and a reopened release authority are compared with the signed deployment manifest by content, so a manifest with the same hub-oracle policy id and one differing field is refused as it was before.

The catalogue replayer's comparison is deleted: it read the string the classifier had already checked. The replay source's policy-id clause is deleted: the protocol script authority digest next to it covers the hub-oracle hash.

Verify and stamp the watcher by hub-oracle policy id

Start-up verifies the release signature over the manifest content and the release bindings, and the verified identity carries hubOraclePolicyId. The durable deployment marker and its two refusals are deleted with the marker.

The ledger store file, persisted observations, the fault decision and queue journals, the rule bundle, the parameter registry and the DA read scope are named or checked by the policy id. The closed-stream DA read retry accepts the 28-byte fingerprint.

Bind fault-proof workflows to the hub-oracle policy id

Workflow identities, deployment bindings, the release finality policy, funding authorities and measurement identities, the rollback cursor and the readiness report carry hubOraclePolicyId (28 bytes) in place of the manifest-id fingerprint and its digest. The CLI flag is --hub-oracle-policy-id.

Comparisons of two values taken from the same verified identity in one process are deleted. Checks of values that arrive from a caller, a file or storage stay.

Stamp and scope the node by hub-oracle policy id

The node database, its deployment-keyed tables, DA publication and announcement rows, the commit worker identity and the DA bond context carry hub_oracle_policy_id where they carried the manifest id or the deployment marker. A database recorded for another policy id is still refused at start.

/protocol-info serves hubOraclePolicyId in place of deploymentMarker, and the public node reads MIDGARD_PUBLIC_HUB_ORACLE_POLICY_ID. The DA runtime and publication manifests no longer repeat the fingerprint as contract_deployment_manifest_id.

The migrations are edited in place: a database created before this change fails the schema checksum and a fresh one is required.

Name the deployment by hub-oracle policy id in the SDK

Availability operation contexts and signed-intent inspection take hubOraclePolicyId (28 bytes) where they took a 32-byte deployment identity. The state-queue authenticated transition, replay checkpoint and correction lock witness records carry hubOraclePolicyId in place of deploymentIdentityDigest.

Identify a deployment by its hub-oracle policy id in core

The deployment manifest loses its content-derived manifestId and the deployment marker is deleted. The hub-oracle policy id, already the deployment identity on L1, is the one identity: deploymentManifestHubOraclePolicyId reads it from the manifest.

The release key signs the digest of the manifest content and the release bindings, so the signature still refuses a manifest that differs in any field. The DA deployment fingerprint is the 28-byte policy id, and the runtime manifest no longer repeats it as contract_deployment_manifest_id. The availability-operation journal names the field hubOraclePolicyId.

Other packages do not typecheck until they follow.

Fault-proof L1 captures read and decode only new history

A capture holds the whole history of each unit it names, and a dispute
captures once per move over hundreds of moves. Each capture read every
history transaction from the follower store, admitted it, and decoded it
again to check unit coverage.

The snapshot authority now takes the transactions the caller already
admitted: the follower source serves one still included at the same point
from them and reads only the rest, so a rollback re-reads what moved.
Facts derived from an admitted transaction's bytes (the units it touches,
the outputs it pays) are derived once and carried to the object the next
admission makes of the same bytes. The case history holds what each
header's captures admitted, so every read under the header shares it,
including the item chain's per-hop read of the thread history.

Say in the runbook which confirmed blocks are passed, waited for or refused

The root-mismatch runbook said every refused block is logged as a root
mismatch; a block whose replay itself is refused is the confirmed-replay
alert, which now also names a merged block committing a held root. A block
is passed for its payload only when every source answers that it holds
none.

Derive a passed block's parent ledger once, and test three confirmed-chain guards

A block passed without a ledger left the next block deriving the same
ledger again, a walk back to the gap and a payload request per block. Only
the lowest block of the walk derives its parent now: above it, a parent
that left no ledger was passed, so its ledger cannot be derived either. A
ledger opened for a passed block is released when a callback throws.

Tests added to tests/replayed-ledger.confirmed.test.ts (14 passed), each
seen red with its guard weakened:
- a confirmed head that starts from another root than its parent's is
  refused after a lookup replayed it: with the parent check skipped for
  blocks replayed here, 'expected true to be false'.
- the head is passed when the ledger it starts from cannot be derived and
  the store holds its own: with the head never passed, 2 failed,
  'expected false to be true'.
- a block above a verified head whose ledger was dropped and whose payload
  no source retains is passed: without the not-found catch the call
  rejects with 'no payload of ...'.
- each payload is asked once: with every block deriving its parent,
  'expected [ ...(3) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]'.

Comments corrected: ensure rejects on a payload a source failed to fetch;
a head not above the verified head is verified from the lowest block the
source knows; the verified-head write is one statement.

Give the watcher's replay keeper its durable verified head

The watcher and the devnet journey pass the verified head kept in their
replayed-ledger store, so a confirmed block is replayed whether or not the
store holds the root it commits, and a restart resumes above the last
verified block. A confirmed block passed without a replay is logged once
as a replayed_ledger_confirmed_unverified warning with its cause.

Tests: tests/fault-proofs/replayed-ledger.confirmed-chain.test.ts, 2
passed: a confirmed head that commits its parent's held root over events
that change the ledger holds the checkpoint and is recorded as the
confirmed root mismatch; a confirmed block below the head whose payload no
source retains is passed and reported once. With the keeper's verify mode
turned off both fail ('expected [] to match object [ Array(1) ]',
'expected [] to deeply equal [ { ...(2) } ]').

Keep the verified head in the SQLite ledger store

One row beside the ledgers holds the confirmed block up to which the
watcher verified the confirmed chain, so a restart resumes above it.

Test: tests/ledger-store.sqlite.test.ts, 'keeps the verified head across a
reopen, and has none before the first write'.

Verify the confirmed chain by block from a verified head

The replay keeper accepted a confirmed head as soon as the store held the
root its header commits. A held root says only that some block's replay
opened it: an empty block commits its parent's root, and so can a block
whose events do not replay to it, so such a confirmed block was never
replayed and no root mismatch was reported for it.

ensure now walks back by headers from the confirmed head to the verified
head and replays every block between them over its parent's ledger,
whether or not the store holds the root the block commits, unless this
process replayed that block and its ledger is still held. The verified
head moves up after each block. The head's payload is always waited for.
A block below the head is passed and reported through onUnverified when
every source answers that it holds no payload of it, or when the ledger it
starts from is neither held nor derivable. A header the source no longer
knows ends the walk and is reported once.

The verified head defaults to one kept in the process; the watcher's
durable one follows.

Tests: tests/replayed-ledger.confirmed.test.ts, 11 passed. Each guard was
weakened in turn and the file went red:
- verify mode off (the old root-keyed skip): 7 failed, 'expected true to
  be false' on the lying head, the block below an honest head and the
  stray parent.
- parent-root check off: 1 failed, 'expected true to be false'.
- verified-head write dropped: 9 failed on the verified-head reads.
- replayed-here skip off: 1 failed, 'expected [ ...(6) ] to deeply equal
  [ ...(4) ]'.
- a not-found head passed instead of waited for: 2 failed.
- any unavailable payload treated as not found: 1 failed.
- a head with no held ledger passed: 1 failed, 'expected true to be
  false'.
